transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Amy Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Peregrine Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Ravi Patel (Security), Lina Zhou (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Peregrine's integration needs across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Focus on SDK support (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks for monitoring. Agreement to share pricing, security docs, and schedule POC scoping.

Topics:
- Current infra and latency targets
- SDK and frameworks (LangChain/LlamaIndex) compatibility
- Gateway/proxy and network constraints for Private/VPC
- Rate limiting, quotas, and burst behaviour
- Observability: token-level telemetry, traces, error logs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Amy Chen: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh quick intros then we'll jump in, Diego and I from Redwood.
[00:06] Maya Singh: Hi all, Maya here, lead for ML infra at Peregrine. We run a mix of customer-facing inference and some internal tooling.
[00:11] Ethan Cole: Ethan, platform team, mostly concerned about deployment and network.
[00:15] Ravi Patel: Ravi from security, I'll be looking at compliance and encryption.
[00:18] Diego Martinez: Great, thanks. Quick agenda - we want to cover integration, SDKs, routing and observability, and then figure next steps.

[00:33] Amy Chen: To kick off — can you give us a sense of current stack and what you want Redwood to do? Hosted for rapid prod, or Dedicated/Private for predictable latency and VPC?
[00:41] Maya Singh: Right now we're using an internal self-hosted cluster for a few models but scaling is tough. Latency targets for customer-facing features are 150ms p50 and not more than 400ms p95 end-to-end across our API. We also have strict data residency and some customers require isolated environments.
[00:58] Ethan Cole: We also want developer ergonomics - our engineers use LangChain and LlamaIndex for retrieval augmented generation flows. SDK support and sample code is important.

[01:12] Diego Martinez: Good call. Redwood has SDKs for Python/Node, and we have integration patterns for LangChain and LlamaIndex. We can provide a small sample repo that shows Retriever + Redwood client + prefix caching.
[01:23] Maya Singh: Awesome, do you have prebuilt connectors for LlamaIndex or is it mostly manual?
[01:27] Diego Martinez: We have example adapters and community contributions. For LlamaIndex we've got snippet that plugs the Redwood client as a llm wrapper; for LangChain there's a chain-of-thought example. We'll share repos.

[01:40] Lina Zhou: On rate limits, we need predictable quotas per-tenant. Can Redwood enforce per-api-key quotas and burst windows?
[01:47] Amy Chen: Yes, per-key quotas and rate-limiting policies are configurable. For Hosted we enforce at the gateway level — you can set steady-state QPS and burst tokens, and we expose usage via the Console. For Dedicated you get more control; we can also deploy a sidecar gateway for stricter tenant isolation.
[02:08] Ethan Cole: Sidecar gateway — that implies we run a proxy in our VPC and talk to Redwood control plane? What's the egress pattern for Private deployment?
[02:17] Diego Martinez: For Private (VPC/on-prem), the control plane can be customer-hosted or we run a private control plane in your network. You can deploy our inference runtime behind your gateway — typically the outbound is only for metrics/optional updates. We do support a completely air-gapped mode too.

[02:34] Ravi Patel: Encryption and keys — do you integrate with our KMS? We need customer-managed keys, HSM optional, and audit logs per request.
[02:43] Amy Chen: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM for Private. Audit logs are available with retention options as an enterprise add-on; they include request metadata, model/version, and token-level usage. We'll share the SOC2 and whitepaper.

[02:59] Maya Singh: Nice. For our POC we want to measure both latency and cost per-token. How do you recommend benchmarking for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:07] Diego Martinez: Typically we run a small benchmark that simulates your request distribution — sequence lengths, concurrency, and retrieval calls. For Dedicated we provision reserved capacity and run stress tests; for Hosted we instrument real workloads or replay logs. We'll provide a benchmark worksheet so you can plug in your traces.

[03:28] Ethan Cole: About the SDK: how does streaming work? We stream tokens to clients now.
[03:33] Amy Chen: Streaming is supported in our SDKs and via the REST/HTTP streaming APIs. We also have server-sent events and websocket examples. For RAG flows, continuous KV cache and prefix caching will help with cost.

[03:47] Maya Singh: LangChain and LlamaIndex sometimes reroute calls and spawn many short connections — will that break rate limit assumptions?
[03:53] Diego Martinez: Good question. We recommend batching at the SDK or a small gateway/proxy on your side that consolidates requests where possible. On our side, we expose metrics to help detect fan-out and you can set per-route quotas.

[04:11] Lina Zhou: Observability — what hooks do you provide? We need traces, token-level billing, and per-model dashboards.
[04:18] Diego Martinez: Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, traces, and error logs. We expose tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry) you can ingest into your existing tracing backend. We also offer webhooks for usage events and an API to pull metrics programmatically.

[04:36] Ravi Patel: About compliance — for customers in EU we need data residency and audit workflows. Do you host in eu-west regions?
[04:44] Amy Chen: Yes, Redwood has regions in EU/NA and can provision Dedicated clusters in region. For Private, you can run the control plane in your region. We also offer data retention controls and deletion APIs.

[04:57] Maya Singh: Pricing — ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted? We'll need numbers to plan the budget.
[05:02] Amy Chen: We'll send you a tailored pricing sheet. High level: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated has a monthly reserved commit with better unit economics for steady loads and predictable latency. We'll include examples in the pricing doc.

[05:18] Ethan Cole: For Private deployments, how much lead time and typical infra footprint?
[05:23] Diego Martinez: Depends on model sizes and throughput. Small POC can run on a single node with 1-2 GPUs; production Dedicated fleet often uses multiple GPU nodes with autoscaling. We'll scope during the POC scoping call.

[05:38] Maya Singh: Integration with our existing gateway — we use Kong + internal auth. Can we put Redwood behind our API gateway?
[05:44] Amy Chen: Yes, common pattern is to use your gateway to handle auth/tenant mapping and forward requests to Redwood. We support JWT/SAML exchanges and can validate tokens at the edge. For tighter control we can deploy a lightweight proxy in your VPC.

[06:00] Diego Martinez: Also to mention: we provide SDK middleware for LangChain that handles chunking, retries, and backpressure. That helps when LLM calls are coming from many parallel retrievers.

[06:12] Lina Zhou: Regarding quotas per-tenant — can we have hard ceilings that drop requests vs soft throttles?
[06:18] Amy Chen: Both. You can configure policy per-api-key: soft throttle with 429 + retry-after, or hard deny. We can also add usage-based routing to fall back to cheaper model variants if you're over budget.

[06:33] Ravi Patel: Audit detail — do audit logs include full prompt content? That's a blocker for some regulated customers.
[06:41] Maya Singh: (overlap) That is important, sorry.
[06:42] Amy Chen: You can configure sensitive data redaction. By default we capture metadata and token counts; full prompt capture is an opt-in with customer consent and additional controls (e.g., encryption at rest with CMK). We'll send the whitepaper with specifics.

[06:58] Ethan Cole: About the LangChain examples — would be great if you had a sample that shows a retriever + Redwood streaming with fallback to smaller model if rate limit hit.
[07:06] Diego Martinez: We do have a canary/fallback pattern sample. We'll include that in the repo. It's a common pattern — detect latency/cost threshold and swap to a quantized variant or smaller model.

[07:20] Maya Singh: If we do Dedicated, how is rollouts handled? We have multiple model versions and want canary deploys.
[07:26] Amy Chen: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and A/B testing by routing policy. You can pin a customer segment to a model version, and we support automatic fallback policies based on error rates or latency SLOs.

[07:40] Ethan Cole: Network egress — for Private we need assurance that no customer data leaves region.
[07:45] Diego Martinez: Understood. Private deployments allow you to keep traffic in-region; air-gapped option is available. For Hosted, we do have regional endpoints; we can document exact egress flows.

[07:58] Lina Zhou: Ok practical POC ask: we want a small pilot serving 5k qps spikes for a 2 hour window and baseline 200 qps. Can Redwood scope that?
[08:05] Diego Martinez: Yes — we'll propose a Dedicated pilot with burst capacity or Hosted with reserved concurrency. We'll use your sample workload to size.

[08:18] Maya Singh: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? We rely on its NodeJS integration for some teams.
[08:23] Diego Martinez: We've seen the same; main issues are too many small requests from connectors. The fix is either batching in the connector or using the Redwood proxy to consolidate. Also ensure your retriever uses top-k and chunking to control context size.

[08:42] Amy Chen: Quick note on SLAs: Dedicated customers can get latency and uptime SLOs in contract. Hosted offers best-effort for self-serve but enterprise customers can upgrade.

[08:56] Ethan Cole: For observability, do you export OpenTelemetry traces or just console?
[09:01] Diego Martinez: Both. We can push traces to your backend or you can pull from our metrics API. Console is convenience but everything is available via APIs and webhooks.

[09:16] Ravi Patel: About pen tests and compliance, we'll need to schedule a security review once NDA is in place.
[09:21] Amy Chen: Absolutely — we'll share our security questionnaire and SOC2 report.

[09:28] Lina Zhou: Any performance numbers you can share for quantized models?
[09:33] Diego Martinez: We have internal benchmarks for 8-bit quantized models showing ~2-3x throughput vs fp16 for certain model families; we'll include model profiles in the onboarding doc.

[09:45] Maya Singh: Great. To close, recap next steps?
[09:50] Amy Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing and dedicated options, security docs, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo, and a benchmark worksheet. We'll schedule POC scoping with your infra and security the week of Nov 8. Any other asks?
[10:04] Maya Singh: That's it for now — thanks.
[10:07] Ethan Cole: Thanks everyone.
[10:09] Ravi Patel: Thanks.

End of transcript.

Notes:
- Shared artifacts referenced: Deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/peregrine-integration), Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/peregrine-workbook), LangChain sample repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples).
